Who owns a row once the round has carried it out

log_next_owner.Rd

The owner after the execution of the version the log describes: the row passes to the newest of the authors who count, log_pending_authors(), which is the referent whose change the round is carrying out. IT included: a change IT wrote and the round carried out makes IT the owner.

Usage

log_next_owner(
  events,
  record,
  creator,
  fields = register_intent_fields(),
  approvers = character(),
  channel_account = NULL,
  current = NULL
)

Arguments

events

The event log, as register_log() returns it.

record

The record id to look at.

creator

Who created the row, as log_creators() answers.

fields

The intent fields.

approvers

The IT accounts whose approval counts on any row.

channel_account

The REDCap usernames that hold the round's token, one or more, or NULL when they are not configured.

current

The row as the round will leave it, a data frame of one row, or NULL when there is no row in hand, for log_pending_authors().

Value

One username; "" or NA_character_ as log_owner() answers them, and NA_character_ too when the log cannot say who the authors are.

Details

The passage is decided once, by the round that carries the change out, after the gate has let it through: what this function reads is a version already approved, and it does not judge the approval again.

The act is judged, not the path that led to it (decided on 2026-10-17). A revocation does not move the row, whether it went through freely or was approved: whoever wrote only request_status = 'revoked' and no other intent field never becomes the owner, even when the version also holds somebody else's change. The row passes to the newest of the other authors who count, and stays with the owner of today when only withdrawals are left.

An author counts in two stretches, and is a withdrawal alone only when every write of theirs that counts, in both, is one. Above the last execution, every write of theirs is read, not only the ones still in the row, as log_revocation_only() reads the others. Below it, an uncovered change, log_uncovered_authors(), is never a withdrawal, which that function leaves out: an author it names changed something the version carried out holds, and can take the row, whatever they wrote above. So a revocation above the execution over an uncovered change by somebody else passes the row to that somebody, and over an uncovered change of their own to its author.

Without the channel's account, channel_account = NULL, no write of owned_by is believed and no row passes: the answer is the one of log_owner(), the creator, or unknown on a row whose channel the log cannot tell.
